record.paper_title: Some problems and conjectures about L2-invariants
record.original_question: Can condensed mathematics be used to extend the present formalism of L2-invariants in a way that sheds light on existing open problems, for example by producing analogues of the group von Neumann algebra over F_p? More broadly, can L2-invariants be applied to a wider class of geometric problems arising from condensed mathematics or analytic geometry?

evidence.quote: In the context of L2-invariants, condensed mathematics poses at least two interesting questions. (1) The theory of L2-invariants heavily relies on techniques mixing algebra and topology or functional analysis. Can condensed mathematics help to extend the current formalism of L2-invariants in a way which sheds light on open problems in the area? For example, are there analogues of the group von Neumann algebra of a discrete group over Fp? (2) Can L2-invariants be applied to a wider class of geometric problems coming from condensed mathematics?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. Let $G$ be a countable discrete group. The group von Neumann algebra $\mathcal{N}(G)$ is the weak closure, in $B(\ell^2(G))$, of the complex group algebra $\mathbb{C}[G]$ acting by left convolution; equipped with the canonical finite trace $\tau(a)=\langle a\delta_e,\delta_e\rangle$, it gives rise to the classical theory of $L^2$-invariants (such as $L^2$-Betti numbers $b_n^{(2)}(X;\mathcal{N}(G))$ of $G$-spaces $X$, and $L^2$-torsion). Condensed mathematics provides a framework in which topological algebraic structures (such as topological abelian groups, modules over topological rings, and locally compact spaces) are replaced by sheaves of abelian groups (resp. modules) on the pro-étale site of a point, yielding a well-behaved abelian category of "condensed" objects in which derived functors of topological constructions behave well, and which makes sense over arbitrary base rings, including $\mathbb{F}_p$.

Problems. 
(1) Construct, using the framework of condensed mathematics, a meaningful analogue over $\mathbb{F}_p$ of the group von Neumann algebra of a countable discrete group $G$: produce a condensed $\mathbb{F}_p$-algebra $\mathcal{N}_{\mathbb{F}_p}(G)$ (together with a suitable trace or dimension function on a class of modules) that plays the role of $\mathcal{N}(G)$ in defining $\mathbb{F}_p$-coefficient analogues of $L^2$-Betti numbers and $L^2$-torsion, and which recovers or interacts with the standard theory when $G$ is amenable or residually finite.

(2) Develop a formalism of $L^2$-invariants for objects of condensed (or analytic) geometry — for instance for condensed/analytic spaces equipped with a $G$-action, or for sheaves on the pro-étale site — that extends the classical formalism for $G$-CW complexes and that can be applied to geometric problems (such as approximation/Lück approximation, Atiyah-type integrality questions, or vanishing conjectures) not accessible to the classical theory.

Determine whether such constructions exist with the indicated properties, and, if so, whether they yield new information about existing open problems in the theory of $L^2$-invariants.
artifact.status_search_result: No published work was found that constructs a condensed-mathematics analogue of the group von Neumann algebra over $\mathbb{F}_p$ or that develops an $L^2$-invariants formalism in the condensed/analytic-geometry setting. The questions appear to be programmatic and open.

status_evidence.title: Some problems and conjectures about L2-invariants
status_evidence.snippet: Problem list including questions on whether condensed mathematics can extend the formalism of L2-invariants and produce analogues of the group von Neumann algebra over F_p.
status_evidence.claim: The questions are posed as open problems with no known resolution.
